findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex, unit 'A people on the march', first paragraph, last sentence (physical p. 9): 'The second, with Augustine, hears in both releases the work of mercy.'
findings.problem: The sentence follows Cassiodorus's two releases: the world's pomps leaving the mind, and release a daemonum turba. A reader therefore takes 'both releases' to mean those two. The second reading's actual join is the one the study draws: Israel's release from Egypt and the debtor's release from his debt are both the work of mercy. The study grounds it on Augustine's 'no man is turned away in heart from this world, unless aided by the gift of the Divine mercy' (sections/30-debt-forgiven-from-the-heart.tex, 'The whole Mass around the parable'). Compression has lost that join, and the second reading's view of the Alleluia is unrecoverable here.
findings.required_result: Name the two releases the second reading joins, for example 'The second hears in Israel's release and the debtor's remission alike the work of mercy, since no one leaves Egypt in heart unless aided by the Divine mercy (Augustine).' Do this without crediting Augustine with the join to the parable.

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex, unit 'Who is the enemy, and what is the armour?', paragraph beginning 'The armour is armatura Dei' (physical p. 6): '... a figure of the spiritual war (In Ephesios III, PL 26, col. 543).'
findings.problem: The concise merges Jerome's two points into one sentence and ends it with a single citation, col. 543. That column now also covers the wars of Israel (David and Goliath, Josue, the Judges, the Kings). research/scope.md records the wars at cols. 545-546, read on the text layer. The study keeps 'col. 543' with the armour-as-Christ clause, and its wars sentence carries no column. The References' 'cols. 543-546' still lets a reader find it, so nobody is misled about the substance, but the claim-local locus is now wrong.
findings.required_result: Cite col. 543 after the armour-as-Christ clause, and cols. 545-546 (or no column) for the wars of Israel.

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex, unit 'A will none resists, and an adversary who asks', paragraph beginning 'The other two readings hear the same two chants' (physical p. 5): 'The third hears Mardochai remind God of "thy portion, which thou hast redeemed for thyself out of Egypt" (13:16)'
findings.problem: Esth 13:16 is outside the Introit (Esth 13:9-11). research/interpretations.md requires unsung context to be marked wherever it is used. The study marks this verse ('in lines the Mass does not sing Mardochai reminds God of ...', sections/40-last-exodus-of-the-church.tex). The concise marks 13:15 in the sentence before but not 13:16. The page-1 map's citation keeps a careful reader from mistaking the verse for sung text, which is why this does not block.
findings.required_result: Carry the mark to 13:16, for example 'The third hears Mardochai, in the same unsung lines, remind God of ...'.

findings.location: sections/concise/02-overview.tex, Anagogical row '(Fromage)' (p. 1); sections/concise/10-commentary.tex 'the continuation of The Liturgical Year' (pp. 6, 8, 9) and 'Fromage hears', 'Fromage sets' and 'Fromage reads' (all p. 10)
findings.problem: The body never says that Fromage is the author of the continuation of Gueranger's The Liturgical Year. A reader of the concise alone meets an unidentified 'Fromage' on page 1 and again on page 10. Between those pages, 'the continuation of The Liturgical Year' reads as if it were a different witness. Only the References entry ('The continuation of Prosper Gueranger, The Liturgical Year (Dom Lucien Fromage)') joins the two names. The study makes the identification in its body (sections/10-each-element.tex, 'Lucien Fromage, continuing Dom Gueranger's The Liturgical Year').
findings.required_result: At the first body mention (p. 6), identify him once, for example 'Dom Lucien Fromage, continuing Gueranger's The Liturgical Year, commenting on this Mass, ...'. After that, use one form consistently while keeping the attribution to the continuation. The overview may keep '(Fromage)'.

findings.location: sections/concise/04-themes.tex, final sentence (physical p. 4): 'The commentary that follows sets the readings' answers beside one another where the texts put the same question to all three.'
findings.problem: This sentence's subject is the document's own commentary, and it describes the editor's method of arrangement. guidance/editorial.md 'State the finding, not the process that produced it' names this form: the guide's own pages as grammatical subject. It occurs once, the preceding sentence already states the finding, and it does not recur as a habit, so it is advisory.
findings.required_result: End the themes on the finding: drop the sentence, or recast it with the texts or witnesses as subject. For example, say that the readings part at the Communion over who the persecutors are and when the judgment comes. Keep the themes ending on physical page 4.

summary: Reviewed the concise study 61-twenty-first-after-pentecost-synthesis (synthesis.tex with sections/concise/01-90). All 16 sealed REVIEW_INPUTS hashes matched. An independent pdflatex build settled on the first pass to a 12-page PDF, SHA-256 6dac0a78aba16c93ba78a9148a162d9aab480388ce89b8bfcacebecebc846b9e, byte-identical to the derive-synthesis artifact, with no overfull, underfull or undefined-reference warnings. Its zref markers put the inventory and the four sense rows on page 1, chronology on page 2, themes on pages 3-4 and commentary from page 5; the apparatus runs pp. 11-12. All twelve pages were inspected rendered. Each reading's distinct answer was recovered from the concise prose before the study was opened. (1) God's government: Gregory's petition and permission (deficeret/proficeret), Thomas's will versus power, and Chrysostom's enemy behind the persecutor. (2) The forgiven man's heart: Chrysostom's receiver who revokes, Augustine's God who calls back, Thomas's per ingratitudinem, and correction without rancour. (3) Time: Augustine's martyrs' plea answered by long-suffering, Chrysostom's girded Passover march, and Thomas's reckoning from tribulation to judgment. Comparison against sections 10/20/30/40/50/80/90 and research/interpretations.md found every controlling claim present. Hilary vs Augustine, Chrysostom vs Augustine vs Thomas on the pardon, and Jerome vs Thomas on the armour are all preserved. The unsung-context labels (Ps 118:84a, Mt 18:21-22, Esth 13:12-17) survive, and the commentators are kept off other Masses. An 8-gram scan found every quotation in the concise already in the study, and the spot-checked paraphrases were also already there; no new source-dependent claim was found. About 44% of the commentary's non-quoted prose is shared verbatim with the study, a condensation rather than a copy. Exact loci checked in tracked payloads: Augustine Enarr. 118.84 (the 'until' comes from the order of the two questions, as the concise says) and 89.3; De serm. Dom. I.22.77; Chrysostom Hom. Matt. 61.4 (the revocation, 'whom by mere prayer') and 61.5; Hom. Eph. 22-24; Thomas Super Matth. 18 (Origenes; remissio efficaciam habet a sacramentis; per ingratitudinem; subiicitur daemonibus); Hilary Caph 5, PL 9 573-574; Gregory Moralia Pref. 14 and 16. Page-2 lookup on the rendered table: the Communion's Ps 118:84 is found in three paired rows. Those rows are 'Occasion date unresolved'; the Psalter collection 'Before c. 165 B.C.'; and David's reign 'Disputed: B.C. 1055-1015', whose place phrase says the reign dates David, not the psalm. The Gospel Mt 18:23-35 likewise pairs three rows, each readable without crossing columns. The event is the parable told at Capharnaum, 'Date unresolved'; the default composition is Palestine, c. A.D. 38-45 and alternatives; the labelled critical comparison is Antioch, 'Post-A.D. 70'. The rows and place phrases are identical to the reviewed study appendix. Limits: the chronology corpus, the rubrics and the study's own source verification were not re-derived beyond these spot checks, and the PG 27 page images and the Corpus Thomisticum Super Iob were not reopened. Verdict PASS, with five advisories.
